Content: Traders work on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange before the closing bell on 29 September 2026.Photograph: Sarah Yenesel/EPAView image in fullscreenTraders work on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange before the closing bell on 29 September 2026.Photograph: Sarah Yenesel/EPAUS economyGood news in US inflation report boosts chances Fed won’t hike ratesTraders see about a 35% chance of an October rate hike, down from ​about 45% following White House pressureGuardian staff and agenciesWed 30 Sep 2026 11.34 EDTLast modified on Wed 30 Sep 2026 16.05 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleGood economic news boosted Wall Street’s main indexes on Wednesday, as a softer-than-anticipatedinflationreading buoyed up hopes that theFederal Reservemight not hike rates as soon ⁠as next month.A commerce department report ⁠showed the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) ​price index stood at 3.4% on an annual basis in August against estimates of 3.7%, per economists polled by Reuters.Separately, second-quarter GDP data – the broadest measure of the economy’s health – showed that theUS economygrew at a solid clip, driven ⁠by robust consumer spending and business investment related to the buildout of AI infrastructure.“The market had been tracing out a bullish formation, meaning the price pattern suggested that any positive catalyst could trigger a move higher and that’s exactly ⁠what happened,” said Sam Stovall, chief investment strategist at CFRA Research.Traders now see a roughly 35% chance of an October rate hike, down from about ​a 45% chance, according to data ‌compiled by LSEG. The Federal Reserve is under pressure to cut rates from the White House afterraising themearlier this month for the first time since 2023.Inflation has emerged as the top issue for voters in the run-up to the midterm elections withDonald Trumpreceiving poor marks for hishandling of the economy.US stock markets rose in early trading, but the S&P ended the day down 0.25% and the Dow fell 0.86%. The Nasdaq ended the day up 0.24%.Despite weakness in September, driven by bond market volatility and elevated oil prices amid the US-Iran conflict, the benchmark S&P 500 and the ‌Nasdaqwere on pace for a second straight quarterly advance, if gains hold.On ​Wednesday, the yield on the 10-year treasury bond held steady at 5.246%, a day after hitting its highest since June 2007. Crude oil prices rose on the day, with the December contract for Brent crude futures moving higher.There was also positive news from the jobs market. ADP, the US’s largest payroll supplier, said private employers added 90,000 jobs in September, higher than expected and up from 36,000 in August.On Friday, the labor department will release its latest monthly jobs tally, which is expected to show a gain of 84,000 for September, down from 162,000 in the prior month.Reuters contributedreportingExplore more on these topicsUS economyInflationUS interest ratesUS unemployment and employment statisticsBondsEconomicsFederal ReservenewsShareReuse this content

title: A ‘freaked out’ US food industry is hitting back at Maha – with social media influencers | Food & drink industry | The Guardian
description: Cross-partisan support in Washington on issues like pesticides and food additives pose a threat to the industry’s bottom line
Author: Rachel Leingang
Headline: Cross-partisan support in Washington on issues like pesticides and food additives pose a threat to the industry’s bottom line
Content: ‘RFK Jr believes chronic illness is primarily caused by processed foods and dyes, exposure to certain chemicals, and poor farming practices.’Composite: The Guardian/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreen‘RFK Jr believes chronic illness is primarily caused by processed foods and dyes, exposure to certain chemicals, and poor farming practices.’Composite: The Guardian/Getty ImagesFood & drink industryA ‘freaked out’ US food industry is hitting back at Maha – with social media influencersCross-partisan support in Washington on issues like pesticides and food additives pose a threat to the industry’s bottom lineRachel Leingangand Riley MesserWed 30 Sep 2026 06.00 EDTLast modified on Wed 30 Sep 2026 12.28 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleSome of the biggest food and agriculture corporations in the US are funding a campaign that pays social media influencers to combat elements of Robert F Kennedy Jr’s Make America Healthy Again platform, according to an investigation by the Guardian and Documented, an investigative watchdog and journalism project.a logo that says documentedThe ascension of RFK Jr to secretary of health and human services has boosted his putative campaign to end chronic illness in the US, which he believes is primarily caused by processed foods and dyes, exposure to certain chemicals, and poor farming practices, along with an overuse of what he falsely claims are dangerous vaccines. The “Maha” movement blends long-running mainstream concerns about food and farm safety with conspiracy theories about everything from medicine to milk. A Maha “summit” in Washington this week will feature JD Vance and several members of Trump’s cabinet.A KFFpollfrom May 2026 reveals that some Maha themes resonate with a broad segment of US adults. About four in 10 say they support the Maha movement, while a majority of the public say there is not enough regulation of pesticides used in agriculture (64%) or of chemical food additives (75%).View image in fullscreenAn Eat Real Food rally at Brazos Hall in Austin, Texas, on 26 February.Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty ImagesCross-partisan support in Washington on some of these issues poses a threat to the food industry’s bottom line – though the Trump administration has largelystopped shortof enacting new regulations.But several large corporations are fighting back. An effort by the Center forFoodIntegrity, an industry-funded non-profit, tracks public sentiment around key issues central to Maha and suggests ways that agricultural interests can counter those narratives by appealing to emotion or scientific reasoning.They call it Gaha: Growing a Healthier America. Documents show the coordinated effort is tracking Maha closely and researching ways to respond to the movement’s claims without alienating its supporters. They are focused on several key areas: seed oils, pesticides, high-fructose corn syrup, regenerative agriculture, organic farming, raw milk/dairy and “big ag”, internal documents obtained by the Guardian and Documented show.The campaign involves deploying social media influencers with significant reach online in an effort to rebuild trust in the industries that the Maha movement has made their target. The Gaha influencer campaign officially launched late last year. In February, CFI compiled a report listing dozens of sponsored posts on platforms such as online blogs, Facebook, TikTok and Instagram about key Gaha subjects. So far, at least six influencers have signed on to the Gaha campaign, reaching a total audience of more than 2.6 million viewers.Influencers who participated in the paid campaign said they saw it as a way to counter misinformation that comes from Maha proponents, many of whom are paid to promote products in the wellness space. Some of the paid posts involved talking to farmers about pesticides or regenerative agriculture, which is the practice of restoring soil health, or explaining what seed oils are to counter claims that they cause a host of health problems.In one July 2025 training video uncovered by the Guardian and Documented, the center explained the goal was to create an “echo chamber” among the food and agriculture industry groups, aligning them behind “the same ultimate message”.“Without this coordinated response, that misinformation [from Maha] risks undermining consumer trust, fueling new regulations and eroding confidence in agriculture as a whole,” said Kelly Leighton, the center’s executive director, in the video.The Center for Food Integrity,formedin 2007, conducts research and public relations campaigns on behalf of the food and agricultural sectors. Theboardconsists of corporate executives from top brands: Bryan Malenius, CFI’s board president, also serves as the director of reputation strategy for public affairs at Chick-fil-A, while other members hold senior positions at companies such as Cargill, Dairy Farmers of America and the National Pork Board. Itsmembers, whose dues pay to keep CFI operating, include groups such as the American Farm Bureau Federation and several state farm bureaus, CropLife America and the National Restaurant Association.CFI created the Gaha campaign in partnership with its member organizations in the farming, agribusiness and food industries, in a bid to re-establish credibility with the public after Maha gained popularity. The American Farm Bureau Federation was also an important driver of the effort: the group’s president, Zippy Duvall, took credit for bringing industry groups together to form the Gaha coalition during aspeechin January 2026.Critiques of the food system, from pesticides to processed foods, have long been the purview of Democrats. With Maha, and Trump’s embrace of Robert F Kennedy Jr, the views have taken hold with many Republicans as well, presenting a broader threat to the agricultural industry.View image in fullscreenRobert F Kennedy Jr at Brazos Hall in Austin on 26 February.Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty Images“That surely freaks the industry out,” said Tom Philpott, senior research associate at the Center for a Livable Future at Johns Hopkins University. “For the industry, they are very concerned about, for want of a better word, a vibe shift.”The Center for Food Integrity declined an interview request, saying in a statement: “At the Center for Food Integrity we recognize the critical link between diet and health. Growing a Healthier America supports an informed dialogue about how the food system can work together to assure a healthy affordable food supply and strong rural communities.”The farm bureau also declined to comment, saying questions should be referred to CFI as it was their project.Inside Gaha messagingIn mid-2025, the Gaha campaign began taking shape: CFI released a variety of resources for industry groups to use as a framework for their communications strategies moving forward.The Guardian and Documented uncovered dozens of pages of internal materials related to this effort, including a “Say This, Not That” guide. It provided highly specific advice about language on key Maha topics, and included an influencer campaign creation guide.Since last May, CFI has also released regular insight briefs, which identify Maha narratives gaining traction in the news and on social media, allowing industry to understand public sentiment shifts and adjust their messaging accordingly.In a brief covering February and March, for example, the summary of online activity about processed foods noted that childhood obesity had reached a new high, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and cited a Canadian study linking ultra-processed foods in early childhood to “adverse behavioral and emotional changes” in children. On the following page, CFI pointed members to new resources to “support” their communications work specifically on the issue of processed foods.View image in fullscreenThe Eat Real Food rally at Brazos Hall in Austin on 26 February.Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty ImagesCFI’s consumer research also directly informs who gets hired to deliver their messaging. An influencer campaign guide outlined preferred messengers for each consumer segment: for audiences who value authenticity, local farmers and wellness enthusiasts were best; for rationalists, scientists and dietitians; and for comfort seekers, CFI suggested lifestyle creators or faith-based voices.Industry donors were invited to contribute hundreds of thousands of dollars to the Gaha campaign. An internal flyer revealed the perks for those who opt to contribute: supporters who pledge up to $50,000 receive regular updates, donors of up to $100,000 participate in quarterly meetings and provide strategic input, and contributors of more than $100,000 earn a seat on the leadership council, with the opportunity to review and approve strategy as well as help secure funding from others.Why influencers got involvedAccording to a12 August briefby the center, the campaign has had impact: Gaha has generated 13.2m impressions online, with more than 1.1m engagements and an 8.74% engagement rate.Influencers who participated in the campaign posted about key topic areas the center wanted to target: raw milk, seed oils, agriculture. Some featured farmers talking about their work and how they balance using pesticides.Slade Wentworth, who has more than 1 million followers on thedadbriefs, his Instagram account, said he participated in the campaign as part of a series he does that helps families “think critically through political and cultural noise”.“In my opinion, many of the loudest voices in the Maha movement and in the food/wellness spaces in general tend to push anti- and pseudo-scientific claims,” Wentworth said via email. “To me, engaging with CFI was an opportunity to present a balanced discussion on topics that overlap with what I’d typically cover” in the series.View image in fullscreenThe Department of Health and Human Services, in Washington DC on 15 September 2025.Photograph: Bill Clark/CQ-Roll Call Inc/Getty ImagesOne of the topics he covered, on the raw milk movement, resonated well with his audience, he said. The comments he received on the work he did for the campaign were “varied and substantive”, a sign that the content “struck a good balance, enabling folks to lean into their perspectives thoughtfully”.The anonymous creator of hydroxide.foodscience, which has more than 300,000 followers on Instagram, made posts about regenerative agriculture, ultra-processed foods and seed oils as part of the paid program. They decided to participate because it was a “uniquely positive spin on food and agriculture”.“It can be difficult for people to sort through the weeds of food and food science and agriculture to really get the facts, so I think that was like a big reason why this campaign resonated with me,” they said. They do not disclose their name on their accounts.Jessica Steier, the CEO of Unbiased Science, interviewed a farmer as part of the campaign to show what modern farming looks like. Unbiased Science received “a modest fee” for the campaign, but kept full editorial and scientific control, Steier said in an emailed statement. The center didn’t script the post or tell them what to say, which would have been a dealbreaker for Unbiased Science, she said. The work was not about defending industry, but about giving people information to make their own decisions, she said.Much of the information amplified by Maha, Steier noted, falls under a “wave of chemophobia”, where people are told they’re being harmed without much evidence. Unbiased Science wanted to counter the fear by showing why farmers use pesticides, that the goal is to use the minimum amounts necessary and what regulations are in place, she said. Hearing it directly from a farmer “does something a fact sheet can’t”, she said.“If anything, the financial incentives are far stronger on the other side of this,” Steier said. “The wellness economy that profits from fear about food and ‘toxins’ is enormously lucrative. Explaining why a preservative is safe is not where the money is. The people being richly rewarded for shaping what Americans believe about their food are not the ones defending the evidence.”Other influencers the center included in its campaign were Happy Strong Healthy, Dietitian Hannah and Veggies and Chocolate. These accounts did not respond to emailed requests for comment.Maha as ‘existential threat’Jerold Mande, a nutritionist who served as deputy undersecretary for food safety at the US Department of Agriculture under Barack Obama, said the campaign sounds like “crisis management”. He has worked for decades to make food policy a priority, but thinks Maha, with its cross-partisan appeal, represents the biggest threat to the food industry that he’s seen. Using influencers to counter Maha, which is in essence a loose grouping of influencers itself, makes sense.“They realize now that they’re facing an existential threat, and their whole business model over the last decades has evolved around, you know, how do we make money?” Mande said.Still, he said, as Maha has charted some wins and made food policy a political priority, it has failed to install regulations that would create meaningful changes.“You’re not going to make progress if you don’t use government’s two powerful levers: funding and rules,” Mande said.Marion Nestle, a molecular biologist and nutritionist who has studied and written about food politics, said food and agriculture groups are always working to protect their industries, so a campaign like this is “nothing new”, especially when Republicans are now talking about agrochemicals. “Of course, they’re going to lobby, and they’re going to do it in absolutely every way they can,” Nestle said.View image in fullscreenThe Department of Health and Human Services headquarters in Washington DC on 11 February.Photograph: Michael M Santiago/Getty ImagesUsing an outright attack on Maha influencers, many of whom are moms whom Nestle believes “really care about their kids”, would not be a good idea, she said, leading to softer and more behind-the-scenes methods to sway opinion.Maha isn’t “getting anywhere” with major changes to the food system, given the refusal to regulate coming from Kennedy and theTrump administration, she said.“Food companies have license to do all the lobbying they want, and they can say whatever they want,” she said. “They don’t have to do anything. Nobody’s making them do anything. Nobody’s holding them accountable for anything.”This article was produced in partnership with Documented, an investigative watchdog and journalism project. Riley Messer is aseniorresearcher at Documented.Explore more on these topicsFood & drink industryTrump administrationRobert F Kennedy JrSocial mediaFoodHealthUS politicsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Arizona State hockey coach on leave after practice that left player fighting for life | College sports | The Guardian
description: Arizona State have placed hockey coach Greg Powers on administrative leave as the school investigates the collapse of a player during an outdoor workout
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Arizona State have placed hockey coach Greg Powers on administrative leave as the school investigates the collapse of a player during an outdoor workout
Content: Matthew Mayich’s family lawyer says the player suffered from external heat stroke.Photograph: Kameleon007/Getty Images/iStockphotoView image in fullscreenMatthew Mayich’s family lawyer says the player suffered from external heat stroke.Photograph: Kameleon007/Getty Images/iStockphotoCollege sportsArizona State hockey coach on leave after practice that left player fighting for lifeGreg Powers taken off duties during investigationMatthew Mayich unlikely to recover, says lawyerAgenciesWed 30 Sep 2026 14.50 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleArizona State have placed hockey coach Greg Powers on administrative leave as the school investigates the collapse of a player during an outdoor workout.Arizona State’s Matthew Mayichcollapsed during an outdoor workoutin August. He suffered from external heat stroke that reduced flow of oxygen to his brain and is unlikely to recover, according to family attorney Rob Carey. Carey said the 21-year-old Mayich had shown signs of distress before his collapse at the workout, which took place in 89F heat. Carey also said there was no cold water tub available, which is often used to treat overheating. The Green Beret in charge of the practice, Tim Ziesel, did not have a contract with the university.My son’s death during a college football workout was preventable. Lessons must be learnedRead more“Our focus continues to be on Matthew and his family, and on our student-athletes to make sure they have the support they need during this time and as the season begins,” ASU athletic director Graham Rossini said in a statement. “We have continued to collect as much information as possible. After thorough and careful deliberation, I believe this is the best move to provide stability for the hockey program.”Powers refused to answer reporters’ questions on the incident last week.Seven players sent a letter to Arizona State president Michael Crow on Monday urging the school to place the coaches involved in the workout on administrative leave until an independent investigation is concluded. The letter also called out discrepancies from an initial inquiry by the university.Mayich’s parents, John and Christina Mayich, issued a statement on Tuesday agreeing with the players that the coaching staff should be placed on leave.“The NCHC supports Arizona State University’s decision to place head coach Greg Powers on leave while the circumstances surrounding Matthew Mayich’s trauma are examined,” the National Collegiate Hockey Conference said in a statement. “Our thoughts remain with Matthew, his family and teammates.”Explore more on these topicsCollege sportsIce hockeyUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Rival clubs feel relegating Manchester City to Championship would not be enough | Manchester City | The Guardian
description: The Premier League will face pressure from Manchester City’s rivals to push for a sanction that will result in a prolonged absence from the top flight
Author: Matt Hughes
Headline: The Premier League will face pressure from Manchester City’s rivals to push for a sanction that will result in a prolonged absence from the top flight
Content: The clouds continue to build over Manchester City, whose Premier League rivals are pushing for very harsh sanctions.Photograph: Phil Noble/ReutersView image in fullscreenThe clouds continue to build over Manchester City, whose Premier League rivals are pushing for very harsh sanctions.Photograph: Phil Noble/ReutersManchester CityRival clubs feel relegating Manchester City to Championship would not be enoughPremier League executives push for severe punishmentCity maintain they are ‘innocent of the accusations’Matt HughesWed 30 Sep 2026 14.55 EDTLast modified on Wed 30 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Premier League will face pressure from Manchester City’s rivals to push for a sanction that will result in a prolonged absence from the top flight after the club were found guilty of more than 100 charges of financial rule-breaking.Executives at a number of Premier League clubs have told the Guardian that a points deduction that would relegate City to the Championship for a single season would be insufficient given the scale of what an independent commission described as the club’s“disguised funding scheme” and “sham commercial deals”, which enabled them to artificially inflate their income by £900m between 2009 and 2018.While the clubs have no involvement in the sanctioning process, the extent of their ill-feeling towards City illustrates the difficulties facing the Premier League as it seeks to conclude a case itbegan investigating almost eight years ago.Manchester City could be forced to pay Premier League up to £50m in legal costsRead moreThe same independent commission thatfound City guiltyof the vast majority of 115 rule breaches will determine their fate at a sanctions hearing pending the outcome of the club’s appeal, which will be heard by a newly convened independent panel.Under new Premier League rules introduced this season,the appeal hearingmust be concluded within 12 weeks of the deadline on Friday for it to be submitted, with the panel given a further 30 days to deliver its judgment, meaning a decision should be reached by the end of January next year.While not confirmed, the sanctions hearing could take place concurrently during the same time period, although it will not be published pending the outcome of the appeal. City could also subsequently appeal against the sanctions imposed by the commission.It is also possible that the club could delay the process further by arguing that the Premier League’s new expedited timescales should not apply given they were only introduced this season, whereas the charges against them are historic.The club hasalready succeeded in delayingthe publication of the commission’s “core decision”, which was finally released on Tuesday following an appeal procedure.As prosecutor, the Premier League is permitted to petition for its preferred punishment at the sanctions hearing, with City also pleading their case, before a decision is taken by the commission.The Premier League’s position on sanctioning will be taken independently of the clubs by the board of directors comprising the chair, Alison Brittain, the chief executive, Richard Masters, and three independent non-executive directors: Mai Fyfield, Dharmash Mistry and Matthew Ryder KC.View image in fullscreenSheikh Mansour (centre) and Khaldoon al-Mubarak (right) have been Manchester City’s owner and chair respectively for the whole period covered by the rule breaches.Photograph: Martin Rickett/PAThe commission has a wide range of sanctions at its disposal including points deductions, transfer embargos and expulsion from the Premier League. Given the scale of City’s offences, according to the independent panel, there are no comparable precedents. City say they are “innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case”.In the first successful profitability and sustainability rules prosecution, of Everton three years ago for a £19.5m overspend, the Premier League pushed for the club to be docked 12 points in the sanctioning hearing, with the independent commission ultimatelydocking them 10 points, which wasreduced to six on appeal.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionMany of the clubs are calling for a far more severe punishment for City given the commission’s conclusion that without the hugely inflated income they would have breached Premier League and Uefa spending limitsin multiple seasons, and will also lobby to ensure that the whole process is concluded before the end of the season.“Relegation to the Championship for one season would be insufficient,” a club source told the Guardian. “The commission has to arrive at a punishment that is proportionate for years of sustained and deliberate cheating, as well as providing a strong deterrent to it happening again.”Building of the Pep supremacy is an era that will be defined by sham-ballRead moreThe Premier League is in a difficult position, as it is also eager to prevent further mass litigation against City by rivals seeking financial recompense.Burnley were awarded £35mat an arbitration hearing earlier this year after suing Everton on the back of their PSR breach, which they claimed led to their relegation at the end of the 2021-22 season, a decision that has set a precedent for clubs claiming compensation following regulatory offences.Manchester United, Arsenal, Tottenham and Liverpool all reserved their rights to sue City in the event of a guilty verdict two years ago, and have already held informal conversations about whether to pursue a claim now the judgment has been published. While those clubs will all arrive at individual decisions, the extent of City’s punishment could prove critical to their thinking.Many of the top-flight clubsremain unhappywith the Premier League’s decision to reach an agreed sanction this year with Chelseaof a £10m fineafter they self-reported the previous owners making unlawful payments to players and agents during the Roman Abramovich era.Explore more on these topicsManchester CityPremier LeagueFinancesBusinessnewsShareReuse this content

title: Quips, slights and a surprise twist: Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury come face to face | Boxing | The Guardian
description: Anthony Joshua revealed he is speaking to Tyson Fury’s uncle Peter ahead of their fight in December as the pair shared some back-and-forth at a press conference in London
Author: Donald McRae
Headline: Anthony Joshua revealed he is speaking to Tyson Fury’s uncle Peter ahead of their fight in December as the pair shared some back-and-forth at a press conference in London
Content: Tyson Fury (left) and Anthony Joshua meet at a press conference in London.Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenTyson Fury (left) and Anthony Joshua meet at a press conference in London.Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/ReutersBoxingQuips, slights and a surprise twist: Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury come face to faceJoshua reveals he is speaking to Peter Fury on trainingFury vows to ‘blast him out’ at London press conferenceDonald McRaeWed 30 Sep 2026 15.15 EDTLast modified on Wed 30 Sep 2026 17.46 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAnthony Joshua has revealed that he is in contact with Tyson Fury’s uncle Peter, in a surprise twist to the buildup between the two former world champion heavyweightswho will finally meet in the ring in Cardiffin December.Peter Fury trained Tyson when he shocked Wladimir Klitschko towin his first world heavyweight title, in 2015. The uncle and nephew fell out soon afterwards, apparently over a financial dispute, and have not spoken in many years.Fury v Joshua fight confirmed for December at Cardiff’s Principality StadiumRead more“I speak to Peter Fury,” Joshua said before the fight’s first press conference on Wednesday evening in London. “He’s willing to help me as well. Yeah, I’ll speak to him [before I fight Tyson Fury].”Asked if he can learn more about Fury from his uncle, Joshua said: “Not about Fury but about our training and how I can approach the fight. This is where I can improve. Everybody’s going to tell me how to win. But the most important person to listen to is myself at this point in my career.”Joshua said he last spoke to Peter Fury about a month ago. “I speak to Matty Harris [the British heavyweight whom Fury Sr trains] quite a lot. Matty Harris comes down for some sparring. That’s how it all comes about. Through Matty and Peter.”Ben Davison will train Joshua for the fight and he, too, has also worked previously with Fury. Davison helped Fury to return to boxing in 2018, after the fighter had been out of the ring with drink and drug problems for three years following his defeat of Klitschko.Fury seemed initially taken aback when he was told that Davison will be in Joshua’s corner. In seemingly genuine surprise, Fury asked: “Is it confirmed? Is he gonna have him?” He paused and then turned to Frank Warren, who has promoted him for years and said, in deadpan style: “That’s deflating, isn’t it, Frank? It is deflating.”Fury soon made clear that his last comment was a joke: “Don’t forget I left Ben Davison to go with SugarHill [Steward] because he wasn’t good enough and this is the same Ben Davison whoAnthony Joshualeft because he wasn’t good enough.”View image in fullscreenPeter Fury (left) trained Tyson Fury when he shocked Wladimir Klitschko in 2015.Photograph: Lee Smith/ReutersAfter Joshua was dropped numerous times andthen stopped by Daniel Duboisin September 2024, he switched from Davison to work with Oleksandr Usyk’s team. Fury, who was in a cheerful mood, said: “When he got knocked out by Dubois it was the same Ben Davison who everyone said: ‘Oh, he’s this, he’s that …’ Now they’re going back to him?“So that gives me encouragement. That gives me happiness. [Joshua] will probably go out there, get told to throw a jab and throw an uppercut and get himself chinned.”Joshua stressed that “it wasn’t so much going to Ben and Peter because they have worked with Fury before”, saying: “The reason why I went with Ben is because he and his team pinpoint things. [Against Dubois] there are things I could have done better so I won’t put all that blame on Ben.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe RecapThe best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“What I’ve got to do is take control of my fight with Fury, but also add their touch. And with these two powerhouses coming together, I think it will be a match made in heaven. Ben and his team are very good at pinpointing certain things leading up to a fight that I can execute and exploit. I believe that they will get me that one step closer to landing the perfect punch to pin Fury to the ground.”At the press conference Joshua called for a minute’s silence, which was impeccably observed, when he rememberedthe close friends he had lostover the past 10 months. Unexpectedly, Fury then spoke respectfully about Joshua as they shared the stage. But Fury did insist that: “I’m going to blast him out. I’m going to catch him and when I do it’s going to be curtains.”Joshua smiled, saying: “I don’t expect anything else from this man than him saying he’s going to render me unconscious.” He then laughed when Fury quipped: “This man is built like an Adonis, I’m built like a blancmange.”Fury turned to Joshua and said: “I hope after this fight we can have a pint of Guinness together.” Joshua paused and then said: “I don’t know if I can trust you.”But the traditional face-off between the two men passed peacefully and calmly, for both fighters know that none of the intrigue and wisecracks will matter when the first bell rings and they leave their corners to face each other and fight.Explore more on these topicsBoxingAnthony JoshuaTyson FurynewsShareReuse this content

title: Jameis Winston is now the New York Giants’ starter. He’s far from a goofball hero though | NFL | The Guardian
description: The quarterback is widely adored on and off the field. Whether he deserves the public spotlight is another question
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The quarterback is widely adored on and off the field. Whether he deserves the public spotlight is another question
Content: Jameis Winston has been named the Giants’ starter after an injury to Jaxson Dart.Photograph: Brooke Sutton/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenJameis Winston has been named the Giants’ starter after an injury to Jaxson Dart.Photograph: Brooke Sutton/Getty ImagesNFLJameis Winston is now the New York Giants’ starter. He’s far from a goofball hero thoughThe quarterback is widely adored on and off the field. Whether he deserves the public spotlight is another questionArif HasanWed 30 Sep 2026 05.00 EDTLast modified on Wed 30 Sep 2026 07.03 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThroughout the NFL’s history, we’ve had our fair share of clown princes. Not too long ago, Rob Gronkowski was the league’s court jester. That history extends back, through Pat McAfee and Chad Ochocinco, past Jared Allen and John Randle to Jim McMahon, Steve McMichael, John Riggins, Alex Karras and Billy “White Shoes” Johnson.There’s probably something deeply insightful to say about the need for goofballs in a sport characterized by militarized order and a seriousness that borders on self-parody, but what’s important now is how we reflect on these chosen merrymakers.The current clown prince is Jameis Winston, who has become the New York Giants’ starting quarterback after a brutal knee injury to Jaxson Dart. Though the Giants have traded for former Vikings first-round pick and third-string quarterback JJ McCarthy, allindications at the momentare that Winston will continue to start.Winston’s persona has always been goofy. His2015 fumble against Oregonin the Rose Bowl was itself an act of unintentional comedy; a Heisman winner who couldn’t help but stumble backwards and flop like a beached whale.That was the culmination of an up-and-down but nevertheless winning season at Florida State, after which the Tampa Bay Buccaneers selected him with the No 1 overall pick in the NFL draft. At the time, Buccaneers general manager Jason Lichtpraised Winston’s leadershipand football character, doubling down on that in 2017 byadding that Winstonwas “the best leader I think I’ve ever been around – in anything”.More than that, Winston is magnetic, effusively charismatic in a way that spinseven his misstepsinto successes. He has turned an awkward pre-game speech about eating Ws intopart of his brandand hasmade lightof an admittedly bizarre incident where he was accused of stealing crab legs while in college.And his playing style matches this persona. He plays bozo ball; he habitually throws the ball deep, assured that someone is down there to catch it. In the past 20 years, 92 quarterbacks have thrown at least 1,000 total NFL passes. The deepest thrower among all of them is Jameis Winston, whose passes have traveled 10.73 yards downfield on average.Of that 92-quarterback group, he ranks sixth in pick-six percentage (0.4%) and third in combined touchdown-interception rate at 8.3%. He is the author ofthe only“30-30” season in NFL history, throwing at least 30 touchdowns along with 30 interceptions. He makes big plays, just not necessarily for the team he plays for.Bears’ 38-year-old backup Case Keenum rolls back the years to ground EaglesRead moreThere is hardly a more charismatic backup in the sport. Fox Sports has recognized that; last year, it made Winston part of its Super Bowl coverage andthen covered that coverage– worth it, evidently, as that approachearned recognition, with some media calling him the trueMVP of the Super Bowlgiven how viral his antics became.This year, Fox Sports decided he would be one of the centerpieces of its World Cup coverage. It was largely asuccess. He’sfunny, appealing and goofy. More than a few people predict that after Winston’s NFL career is over, he’s going to be a media megastar. They may be right.---Sir John Falstaff is an intriguing character in Shakespeare; one of the most beloved fools in the canon, Falstaff’s indiscretions are often overlooked by those who adore him. Falstaff engages in armed robbery, takes bribes from nobles, steals valor, purposefully endangers the poor and steals their wages on top of it.Winston is no fictional character, however. And no analysis of his lovable on-screen persona is complete without addressing his alleged treatment of women.When it comes to off-field indiscretions, Winston is best known for an incident where he is alleged to have assaulted Erica Kinsman in December 2012 during his time at Florida State, something Winston denies. To say authoritiesbotched the investigationwould be a disservice to the concept of botching.Police are alleged to have warned Kinsman tostop pursuing a claim, saying her life would be “made miserable” because Tallahassee was a “football town”. Later, we would learn that the lead investigating officer had been employed as private securityfor the Seminole Boosters, a fundraising arm for Florida State athletics.FSU would later settle a lawsuitthat Kinsman had brought over the allegations. Winston was never charged with a crime over the allegations.Meanwhile, Winston was the subject of another allegation at FSU after a woman who had sex with him reported to a victim’s advocate that the encounter was “of such a nature that she felt violated or felt that she needed to seek some type of counseling for her emotions about the experience”. While the woman did not accuse Winston of rape, some outletscharacterized the incidentas another allegation of sexual assault. A prosecutor said that based on what she was told of what happened, Winston had not committed a crime.When the Buccaneers drafted Winston, they claimed to have conducted a thorough investigation into his character. Theyinterviewed 75 peoplewith experience of Winston. They never made contact with Kinsman or her attorney. “If he wasn’t a good guy, we wouldn’t have used the first pick on him,” Licht said.A year later, Winston was accused of groping an Uber driver bygrabbing her crotch.The NFL ultimately concluded that Winston touched the driver in a sexual manner, discounting testimony from Winston’s friends giveninconsistenciesin witness statements from those the quarterback claimedwere with himat the time. Winston was not criminally charged over these allegations either. While not admitting guilt,he said: “I would like to say I’m sorry to the Uber driver for the position I put you in. It is uncharacteristic of me and I genuinely apologize.”This series of allegations background something revealing and concerning that he told a group of elementary school kids a year after the alleged incident with the Uber driver. There to preach self-confidence, he said to the children, “All my young boys, stand up. The ladies, sit down … We strong, right? We strong! We strong, right? … Now a lot of boys aren’t supposed to be soft-spoken … One day, you’ll have a very, very deep voice. But the ladies, they’re supposed to be silent, polite, gentle. My men, my men [are] supposed to be strong.”Winston settled privately with Kinsman and the Uber driver in civil cases andhe did apologizefor what he had said to the schoolchildren.His defenders will point out that most of the controversies around Winston – the bulk of negative press surrounding him – were a decade or more ago. What are we to do with them today?But as his media profile expands, these incidents mattermorethan they did when he was only playing. At some level, his primary job is to play football; relay the play in the huddle, call audibles at the line, read defenses after the snap and deliver the ball to the intended receiver.It’s a job that comes with attention and a public profile, but it is not fundamentally reliant on whether he is a good role model. In the media, however, his jobishis personality. He is cast as likable and approachable and so our understanding of his behavior becomes ever more important.And while Winston has never been charged with crimes over the allegations against him, he has never expressed sympathy for the ordeal Kinsman went through – the death threats and harassment she endured. In fact, the one person he seems most worried about is someone else accused of sexual assault.In 2024, he came to the defense of his then-teammate Deshaun Watson after he had been booed by his own fans at the Cleveland Browns. “I’m very upset with the reaction to a man that has the world against him for the past four years,” Winston said. It’s fair to say that many Browns fans weren’t just against Watson because he is a bad quarterback but because he has been accused of sexual assaultby dozens of women. (Watson never faced criminal charges over the allegations but the NFL suspended him for most of the 2022 season after its own investigation. He alsoreached out-of-court settlementswith nearly two dozen of his accusers, without an admission of liability.)Every charming quote from Winston shared across platforms – and there are dozens, includingmore than onefrom this last weekend before and after the Giants’ win over the Titans that the medialapped up– serves as a reminder that sports media writ large appears to value those who have been accused of sexual assault rather than survivors, matching a pattern we seem to see in college: there’s evidence that studentsaccused of committing sexual assaultoften receive special treatment and benefit academically, socially and professionally after being accused.Moreover, there was never a reckoning for Winston as there has been for some other high-profile athletes. No one is required to forgive Michael Vick, who was jailed for his part in a dog-fighting ring, but it is undeniable that he not only served time, butdid worktoimprovewelfare forcountlessanimals bothpubliclyandprivatelyyearsafterhe returned to the spotlight.This does not mean Vickdeservesa public spotlight, but rather that a precondition to his entry into public life was to do work. Not only have we refused to institute that kind of standard for other types of allegations, we’ve proactively promoted charismatic examples that suggest the opposite.In literature, the fool is often a harmless figure – comic relief to lighten an otherwise serious story. We should make sure our real-life jesters are the same.Explore more on these topicsNFLNew York GiantsUS sportsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: WNBA playoffs: Caitlin Clark shines in Fever win as A’ja Wilson confronts fan after Cunningham foul | WNBA | The Guardian
description: The All-Star guard scored 27 points, had 15 assists, reached another milestone and provided the energy on both ends of the court
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The All-Star guard scored 27 points, had 15 assists, reached another milestone and provided the energy on both ends of the court
Content: Caitlin Clark celebrates during the second half of Tuesday’s game.Photograph: Michael Conroy/APView image in fullscreenCaitlin Clark celebrates during the second half of Tuesday’s game.Photograph: Michael Conroy/APWNBAWNBA playoffs: Caitlin Clark shines in Fever win as A’ja Wilson confronts fan after Cunningham foulClark has 27 points and 15 assists in Indiana winWilson assessed technical foul after confrontationAssociated PressTue 29 Sep 2026 22.44 EDTLast modified on Wed 30 Sep 2026 08.55 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAll Caitlin Clark wanted was one more chance to play this season. She delivered a masterpiece. The All-Star guard scored 27 points, had 15 assists, reached another milestone and provided the energy on both ends of the court to help keep the sixth-seeded Indiana Fever’s postseason alive with a 99-89 victory over the defending WNBA championLas Vegas Aces. Kelsey Mitchell added 26 points as the crowd chanted “M-V-P” throughout the game.WNBA playoffs: No 8 Liberty spring historic upset to take down No 1 seed LynxRead moreIndiana evened the best-of-three series at 1-1. Game 3 will be played Thursday at Las Vegas.Clark became the first player in league history to produce a points-assists double-double in the first half of a playoff game. She had 14 points and 11 assists in the first 20 minutes, and it wasn’t just her scoring or passing that impressed.“I thought her energy from start to finish – I mean a double-double in the first half – was pretty incredible,” coach Stephanie White said. “The way she moved the ball, attacked from multiple positions ... You always expect to be able to make shots and facilitate. But I thought how she managed the game was really good and her defensive energy I thought was terrific. It’s what we need from her.”What the Fever and Aces didn’t need was the fourth-quarter incident between a fan and four-time league MVP A’ja Wilson. The two appeared to be pointing and shouting at one another after Sophie Cunningham drew a foul.Wilson walked toward the seatsand two teammates, an assistant coach and security intervened to separate the scrum.“If I see a man come at me, taking steps towards me and pointing at me ... I don’t give a damn what you said ... That is unacceptable … I’m not for that shit,”Wilson said after the game.When speaking to Aces coach Becky Hammon fter the game, Wilson said: “No way he does that to LeBron [James].”Wilson was assessed a technical foul for stepping off the court but was not ejected. The man was escorted out by security but was allowed to return because the Fever said he did not violate the fan code of conduct policy.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Weekly for the 2026 WNBA seasonSign up toWNBA 30A limited run women’s basketball newsletter dedicated to the league’s historic 30th season.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“I didn’t exactly see what happened, I kind of saw the aftermath,” Hammon said. “I’ve never A’ja Wilson go like that so whatever was done I can tell you she felt very disrespected in that moment. I’ve never seen her really react like that ever, so whatever it was, it doesn’t have any place, I don’t think in an arena.”The incident seemed to motivate Las Vegas, who were trailing 90-79 when the incident happened at the 4:10 mark, and when Clark fouled out with 2:45 to play, the Aces got as close as 92-87. But the Fever managed to hang on.“The way I looked at it, your back’s up against the wall,” Clark said. “This is the only opportunity you’re guaranteed to have is these 40 minutes, and you know you’re going to go down swinging if you’re going to lose. But I think we had the mentality like this was one we were going to win, no matter what and do it for our fans.”Explore more on these topicsWNBAIndiana FeverLas Vegas AcesBasketballUS sportsCaitlin ClarkShareReuse this content

title: USMNT youth shines again in contentious 4-2 win over Chile | USA | The Guardian
description: Sebastian Berhalter scored the US’s opener and assisted on the winner in a contentious match that ended in scuffles
Author: Pablo Iglesias Maurer
Headline: Sebastian Berhalter scored the US’s opener and assisted on the winner in a contentious match that ended in scuffles
Content: The US have now won both of their first two games of the international window.Photograph: Jeff Roberson/APView image in fullscreenThe US have now won both of their first two games of the international window.Photograph: Jeff Roberson/APUSAUSMNT youth shines again in contentious 4-2 win over ChileSebastian Berhalter scores and assists on winnerTwo scuffles between teams erupt as match endsJulian Hall, Mathis Albert set records for youngest scorersPablo Iglesias Maurerat Energizer ParkTue 29 Sep 2026 22.18 EDTLast modified on Wed 30 Sep 2026 13.55 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleRiding goals from Sebastian Berhalter, Julian Hall, Chris Richards and 17-year-old newcomer Mathis Albert, the US men’s national team beatChilein St Louis on Tuesday night 4-2. The US were shaky at times but used a blend of regulars and newcomers to get the job done, with Albert becoming the youngest-ever goalscorer for the US men with his insurance goal in stoppage time, and Hall becoming the youngest US men’s player to score in each of his first two games.The game ended with an example of the collective identity a young US group has managed to forge in their first World Cup window, minus major figures like Christian Pulisic, Weston McKennie, and Folarin Balogun. When goalkeeper Brian Schwake fell on the ball as stoppage time ticked over, Chile forward Leandro Hernández left a kick in on the Nashville SC goalkeeper. Richards took exception, confronting Hernández, setting off a group confrontation that cleared both benches and saw US manager Mauricio Pochettino jump in to the middle of the fray to try and calm things down.“We have each other’s back. We have 26 guys that are ready to be there at any moment,” Berhalter told TNT afterward. “When you do stuff like that, there’s gonna be repercussions.”The 49th-ranked Chileans are far removed from their glory days, the stretch of years in the 2010s that saw them win back-to-back Copa Américas and advance to the knockout rounds of the 2010 and 2014 World Cups. Interim manager Nicolás Córdova has started the process of leading the Chileans through a generational turnover as they build towards 2030.Pochettino: Manchester City verdicts show fans ‘lived through an era of deception’Read moreOn Tuesday, Córdova was without the services of Chile captain Gabriel Suazo, one of a pair of his players red carded in their brutally physical 1-0 loss to Canada last weekend. Still, they proved a tougher challenge for the US than Peru,whom the US beat 4-1in the first match of the window three days earlier.Berhalter’s goal came 37 minutes in and was well worked. Sergiño Dest’s combination play at the near sideline pulled several defenders out of position; Hall smartly stepped over Dest’s ensuing cross as it traversed the area and found the Middlesbrough midfielder 10 yards from goal. Berhalter – who was excellent throughout the evening and assisted on the match-winner from a corner kick – drove his effort low into the goal at the near post.“He is a player that the commitment, the energy, everything he does is for the badge, for the national team, for the teammates,” Pochettino said. “He is a very good role model for the players that arrive the first time or maybe are watching from home, in the way we expect the players to behave. The quality he has – the delivery on set pieces, scoring goals, can play from the left, from the right, box to box or a holding midfielder, or like a No 10 from different positions. Always he’s happy to do anything for the national team. These things are priceless. To have a player like him is priceless.”Hall was once again positioned well on his 51st-minute goal, rising above his defender 10 yards from goal to meet a Gio Reyna cross before sending a perfectly placed, glancing header towards the near post. As with Berhalter, it was the Red Bull New York forward’s second goal in as many games.The US arrived in St Louis fresh off the dismantling of Peru, a match that saw 11 US players make their senior debut, just one shy of an all-time record. Pochettino made 10 changes from that match, and while Tuesday’s XI may have lacked the sheer youth of that group, it had no lack of debutants: goalkeeper Chris Brady made his first-ever start, as did Hall, Adri Mehmeti, Neil Pierre, Brooklyn Raines and Frankie Westfield.View image in fullscreenThe match ended with two scuffles between players, the first set off when goalkeeper Brian Schwake was kicked by a Chilean player.Photograph: Jeff Roberson/APTuesday’s starters lacked polish at times – particularly while defending – with the US ceding the lion’s share of first-half chances to Chile. They lacked sharpness going forward, as well; 20 minutes in, Hall was sprung through clean on goal by Berhalter. The Red Bulls attacker rounded Chile keeper Lawrence Vigouroux and turned towards an open goal but couldn’t keep his angled attempt on frame from 12 yards out.Brady looked shaky when asked to control proceedings in the penalty area and was saved by the crossbar twice in the first half. Berhalter’s goal came shortly thereafter.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Twice weeklySign up toSoccer DeskJonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionYet Chile answered just before half-time, off a corner kick which neither Brady (nor any US defender, for that matter) took command of, leading to a frantic goalline scramble. After several thwarted attempts, Chile defender Diego Ulloa finally found an opening in the madness and equalized. Brady was replaced by Schwake at half-time.Just minutes into the second half, Chile struck again. Westfield badly misplayed a header in his own half, one which fortuitously fell at the feet of Maximiliano Gutiérrez, who sprinted forward and hit a bending effort around the outstretched arms of Schwake. Hall quickly equalized.In playful moments, the USMNT’s new youth movement is already paying offRead moreIn the 72nd minute, Richards found the winner when he met Berhalter’s brilliantly struck corner near the penalty spot, heading it home with authority. Albert’s effort came in stoppage time as he crashed goalwards and tapped the ball home off the crossbar; the game quickly devolved shortly afterwards into a shoving match.On a night where US Soccer honored longtime USMNT captain Tim Ream’s retirement, Antonee Robinson wore the armband for the US. Pochettino said earlier in the week that he wants to waste little time in establishing Ream’s replacement as captain for the US’s push towards the 2030 World Cup, but he seemingly hasn’t decided yet; midfielder Tyler Adams got the nod against Peru.The US will face a pair of even stronger opponents to close out this international window, traveling to Phoenix, Arizona to face Mexico on 3 October before facing Canada in St Paul, Minnesota three days later.Explore more on these topicsUSAChileUS sportsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: WNBA playoffs: No 8 Liberty spring historic upset to take down No 1 seed Lynx | WNBA | The Guardian
description: Jonquel Jones had 21 points and 13 rebounds and the No 8 seed New York Liberty beat the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx 87-71 in Game 2 of their WNBA playoff series
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Jonquel Jones had 21 points and 13 rebounds and the No 8 seed New York Liberty beat the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx 87-71 in Game 2 of their WNBA playoff series
Content: Sabrina Ionescu and Pauline Astier celebrate a Liberty three-pointer against the Lynx.Photograph: Heather Khalifa/APView image in fullscreenSabrina Ionescu and Pauline Astier celebrate a Liberty three-pointer against the Lynx.Photograph: Heather Khalifa/APWNBAWNBA playoffs: No 8 Liberty spring historic upset to take down No 1 seed LynxNew York are first No 8 seed to beat first seedLiberty ease to 2-0 series victory over MinnesotaAssociated PressTue 29 Sep 2026 22.55 EDTLast modified on Wed 30 Sep 2026 08.37 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleJonquel Jones had 21 points and 13 rebounds and the No 8 seedNew York Libertybeat the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx 87-71 in Game 2 of their WNBA playoff series on Tuesday night to advance to the semi-finals.Breanna Stewart added 21 points and Sabrina Ionescu had 18 to help the Liberty become the first No 8 seed to eliminate a No 1 seed in the league’s 30-year history. TheWNBAhas undergone a number of different playoff formats, and in many of them, it wasn’t possible for those seeds to match up. However, in 2022 the league changed to the current iteration in which the top-eight teams play in the quarter-finals.“I feel like we had an advantage in our size against them, and I wanted to make my impact early,” the 6ft 6in Jones said after the game. “If a shot is going up I felt like I had to be in the paint and set the tone for the night.”WNBA playoffs: Caitlin Clark shines in Fever win as A’ja Wilson confronts fan after Cunningham foulRead moreNow, New York await the winner of the Atlanta-Washington series. The Dream are up 1-0 and play at Washington on Wednesday night. The semi-finals begin Sunday.A year after losing in the first round to Phoenix after going up 1-0 in that series, New York were determined to avoid a repeat.The Liberty were up five points after one quarter, and scored nine of the final 11 points in the second quarter to go up 49-37 at the break.New York were up 52-39 with 6:26 left in the third when Stewart drove to the basket and was hit in the face by Olivia Miles as she tried to block the shot. Stewart was down for a minute as the officials reviewed the play and upgraded the play to a Flagrant-1 foul. As Stewart walked off the court, she raised her hands to the sellout crowd of 17,593, who serenaded her with “M-V-P” chants. Stewart hit both free throws.Minnesota couldn’t get closer than seven points the rest of the way.The Lynx’s season ends in disappointment again. Minnesota had the best regular-season record, but couldn’t put it together against New York. On Monday, Cheryl Reeve won the league’s Coach of the Year and Miles was a unanimous choice for Rookie of the Year.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Weekly for the 2026 WNBA seasonSign up toWNBA 30A limited run women’s basketball newsletter dedicated to the league’s historic 30th season.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionMiles struggled in both games against New York. She had five points, missing seven of her eight shots in 17 minutes, on Tuesday night and was benched for most of the second-half. The Liberty’s size and ability to protect the rim bothered the stellar first-year player. During the regular season, Miles averaged 19.8 points and ‌6.0 assists.“I thought the playoffs would be hard for our team, regardless of who we were playing in the first round,” Reeve said. “We probably needed a little better matchup to do some of the things that we did all season long, but that’s not how it works.”Courtney Williams scored 18 points and Napheesa Collier added 14 to lead the Lynx.Explore more on these topicsWNBANew York LibertyMinnesota LynxBasketballUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘A lot of lies’: Ireland manager hits out over coverage of Bazunu exit from Israel game | Republic of Ireland | The Guardian
description: The Republic of Ireland manager, Heimir Hallgrimsson, claimed ‘a lot of lies’ were told over Gavin ⁠Bazunu’s decision to withdraw ⁠from the Nations League ​games against Israel
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The Republic of Ireland manager, Heimir Hallgrimsson, claimed ‘a lot of lies’ were told over Gavin ⁠Bazunu’s decision to withdraw ⁠from the Nations League ​games against Israel
Content: Protesters march in Dublin demanding the cancellation of Ireland’s Nations League matches against Israel.Photograph: Nadia Caimi/JNA/Zuma Press/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenProtesters march in Dublin demanding the cancellation of Ireland’s Nations League matches against Israel.Photograph: Nadia Caimi/JNA/Zuma Press/ShutterstockRepublic of Ireland‘A lot of lies’: Ireland manager hits out over coverage of Bazunu exit from Israel gameKeeper pulled out of Nations League games with IsraelHallgrímsson confident Sunday’s rematch will go aheadReutersWed 30 Sep 2026 10.55 EDTLast modified on Wed 30 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Republic of Ireland manager, Heimir Hallgrímsson, has claimed “a lot of lies” were told over the goalkeeperGavin Bazunu’s decision to withdrawfrom the Nations League ​game against Israel last weekend, and he does not anticipate any problems with the second match against them going ahead on Sunday.Ireland are one of Europe’s most outspoken critics of Israel’s war in Gaza, and protests calling for the team to boycott the fixture prompted Bazunu to pull out of both games between the two countries.Israel captain stokes feud by saying ‘our country is 10 times better than Ireland’Read moreThe match last Sunday,which Ireland won 3-0, went ahead after a majority of their squad voted to play on the eve of the away fixture in Hungary. Media reports indicated that the squad was fractured after the meeting and vote, and that Bazunu had been insulted by teammates over his decision.The goalkeeper is available for the home game with Austria on Thursday, but will not take part on Sunday in the rematch with Israel, which the Football Association ‌of Ireland has moved to Serbia behind closed doors.“Gavin is a great lad, I’ve always had a good relationship with him and it’s probably tougher for him than the other players, but they have really welcomed him,” Hallgrímsson told a press conference on Wednesday.“There’s been a lot of lies said around all of this, but we welcomed him back and he’s taking part. Amazing, I think it shows his character, as well, to be with ‌us. So I want to give him praise for that. I want to give the players praise for how welcome they have been with him,” he added. Life goes on. He’s a part of this group and I think that shows how strong the bond is between these players that even a thing like this is not breaking us.”The Ireland midfielder Finn Azaz has also been the centre of attention given his Israeli heritage, and remained on the bench for the win against Israel. Hallgrímsson was asked if Azaz would be involved in the fixture on Sunday. “We are focusing on this one [against Austria], you can probably ask me that question later on,” the manager said.“Finn has shown incredible emotional control and awareness. He probably is one of the people I admire the most in how he conducted himself in all of this.”The ‌game against Austria in Dublin on Thursday is expected to bring further protests over Ireland’s decision to play Israel. Hallgrímsson said: “I am focused on football, I’ll let others think about security. The FAI has said we are playing both games and we will fulfil that. It has been really, really tough, but I surely think that in time we will have seen that we took more right decisions than wrong ones.”Explore more on these topicsRepublic of IrelandIsraelNations LeaguenewsShareReuse this content

title: Building of the Pep supremacy is an era that will be defined by sham-ball | Manchester City | The Guardian
description: Guardiola’s success at Manchester City was underpinned by financial cheating. Now he can only double down on his adherence to the owners
Author: Barney Ronay
Headline: Guardiola’s success at Manchester City was underpinned by financial cheating. Now he can only double down on his adherence to the owners
Content: Pep Guardiola lifts the Premier League at Brighton in 2019 but all his successes at Manchester City are now tainted by the guilty verdicts.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianView image in fullscreenPep Guardiola lifts the Premier League at Brighton in 2019 but all his successes at Manchester City are now tainted by the guilty verdicts.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianManchester CityBuilding of the Pep supremacy is an era that will be defined by sham-ballGuardiola’s success at Manchester City was underpinned by financial cheating. Now he can only double down on his adherence to the ownersBarney RonayWed 30 Sep 2026 16.00 EDTLast modified on Wed 30 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on Google“Do you know the question that you are asking me? Today, do you honestly think it is my job to make this kind of question happen …” Cut to the long, painful pause. Chuck in a deep, shaming stare, eyes that have suddenly become death rays of betrayal and disgust andPep Guardiolahimself transformed from a man cheerfully toasting his own FA Cup final victory to a grizzled chief detective addressing a room full of convicted perverts.Guardiola had the wind entirely at his back at this point, sitting in the Wembley press room an hour afterManchester City’s 6-0 defeat of Watford in May 2019. Success drowns out every other noise in football. To be good is also to begood, noble, virtuous. History is written by the domestic treble winners. Right up until the moment it isn’t.Rival clubs feel relegating Manchester City to Championship would not be enoughRead moreThe question in question was asked by Rob Harris of the Associated Press. It was basically this: information is now in the public domain that suggestsRoberto Mancini received a second salary from Abu Dhabiwhen he was City manager. Mancini was one of Guardiola’s immediate predecessors. So had he, Pep, ever received two salaries?Even as Harris was asking this he was interrupted by City’s press officer, saying: “We’re not going here,we’re really just not going there.” A simple “no” would have done the job. Instead the exchange ended with another beautifully executed mad-dog stare from Guardiola; not angry, just sad and disappointed. But also, let’s be honest, really angry as well.Fast forward to this week and a clip has been doing the rounds of the same Rob Harris, now of Sky News, and still the same perky, questing figure. Harris is approaching Ferran Soriano this time, Pep’s key man through that era, and asking the same entirely legitimate things, with a very different outcome. “The Premier League maintains you cheated for nearly a decade … is all this success, as the Premier League says, based on sham contracts?”There is no glare in return now, no outrage, no flushed moral high ground. “Thank you, thank you,” Soriano mutters, with the look of a man caught shoplifting a Twix at the local primary school fete, followed by a mute, fumbling exit.Sunlight. Scrutiny. Awkward questions from awkward people. It turns out these are still the best disinfectant. Just as it turns out “the question” was the only one worth asking in that room in 2019. Not that anyone agreed at the time. Predictably enough the comments on social media were about scum, bias, the press as a national embarrassment. Even other journalists held a perfumed kerchief to their noses, suggesting this was all a non-issue because, er, the club had just won a treble.It turns out the exact opposite was true. It was entirely the right moment to ask this question. That Cup final win came at the end of the main period of shammery. It was in many ways its unholy coronation. There was an industrial-scale embarrassment in that room. But it wasn’t the person asking the questions.View image in fullscreenThe sports correspondent Rob Harris confronts Manchester City’s chief executive, Ferran Soriano, in Copenhagen.Photograph: Sky NewsThere is an obvious problem with the City story at this stage. It’s just too big. There is too much to say, an entire Dickensian multiverse interlayered with oddities and moments of jaw-drop. This is not, repeat not, a media story. And yet it kind of is a media story. After all, it was media scrutiny and the efforts of the hacker Rui Pinto that first winkled it out. As such, Harris deserves his moment of grace, living proof that it’s culturally vital to keep on asking questions, the same Rob Harris I have seen grilling Vladimir Putin about corruption on the hoof in Zurich, and also walking into a pillar at the World Cup in São Paulo while running off with his laptop to ask someone else something else, a man so deeply locked into the news cycle even reinforced stadium infrastructure doesn’t register.It is also worth mentioning at moments like this Nick Harris, AKA Sporting Intelligence, who has kept going at this story relentlessly despite an unusual degree of abuse, harassment and threats, and who has every right to feel vindicated, part of a world where we can still hold power to account, where a cat can look at a king. But for now the real object of interest in this exchange is, of course, the person on the other end of it. Welcome to the stage once again Pep Guardiola, the public face of the club for the past decade.What did Pep know? This is more than just football legacy chat. It relates to pretty much everything here, the true nature of the club, of elite football itself, and more basic things like truth, spectacle and human nature. Is believing the assurances of others any kind of defence, given Guardiola was in the perfect position to ask questions of his own? Is any kind of deniability plausible here?Andy Burnham admits to ‘concern’ if Manchester City lose their owners after guilty verdictsRead moreThe other significant statement from Guardiola in that time came after City’s two-year ban from theChampions Leaguefor a serious breach of Uefa’s financial fair play rules wasoverturned by the court of arbitration for sport. “We didn’t break the rules. We played the same rules as all the clubs in the Premier League,” was Guardiola’s conclusion, which seemed pretty silly at the time, given time-barring of offences was key to that decision. How does it look now?To this day Guardiola’s stance remains slavish adherence to the promises of his paymasters, as evidenced by his first statement on the matter on Wednesday. Guardiola sayshe will be getting through the current unpleasantnesswith the club and its fans, sticking together as always. But were you together, really? Because City’s fans have some urgent questions of their own now. The majority believed what they were told, and put their faith in the “irrefutable body of evidence” schtick. That ring binder of truth really is going to have to do a lot of instant high-speed kung fu when it finally comes screeching into the appeal room on its trail bike. Not to mention explaining where it’s been over the past three years of information exchange.Guardiola will face his own questions too, and on a level that will hurt him. The coach who only stays for three or four years stretched this out to a full decade at a club where 80% of that time was spent under a cloud of sham contracts and casual hubris. Through all this he had a deeply personal relationship with his chair, Khaldoon al-Mubarak. The pair of them are seen whispering tenderly in the recent Prime documentary, in which Guardiola is presented as the most genuine and heartfelt of truth-seekers, a lone castaway on Integrity Island, Jedi-like in a tailored hoodie, eyes brimming with tears as he talks feelings and eternal truths, like a dad in the pub on Christmas Eve.View image in fullscreenKevin De Bruyne joined Manchester City from Wolfsburg for £51m in 2015.Photograph: Ash Allen/EPAIn his farewell hagiographies, Guardiola was routinely described as the greatest modern manager. He invented the Messi role for Messi. He reimagined the basic texture of the sport in this country. If this guy isn’t good, nobody’s good. On the other hand, the only logical conclusion on the facts as they stand is that all his City trophies were won with the benefit of concerted macro-cheating.During the period embraced by the charges, City’s net spend on transfers was, according to Transfermarkt, almost £400m more than Manchester United in second place, and five times as much as Liverpool and Arsenal. From 2016 to 2018, the key period in building the Pep supremacy, they massively outspent every other team. After which they won the league on the final day or by a single point three times. There were little things throughout, like digging out an extra £25m for Kevin De Bruyne, stretching those fine details in your direction. How is it possible not to see that success as unrelated to stolen margins? This is an era that will now be defined by sham-ball, trophies hoisted with a hand behind your back and a thumb on the scale.Pep can only double down now and ride this to the end. His life’s work, his vast and all-consuming reputation is at stake. “We will get through this together,” he says in Wednesday’s statement. Well, you have no choice now, Pep. Wherever that destination might be.There are others who must now enter the matrix of who knew what. Soriano, subject of the second Harris grilling, is utterly bound up in this. He’s there right at the start, speaking to us in the leaked emails published by Der Spiegel. “We will need to fight this,” Soriano writes in one leaked memo, “and do it in a way that is not visible.” Hmm. How’s that part working out?Soriano’s own pre-City past has already been sliced and diced by those who wish to see a pattern. For the record, and as a basic statement of fact, he was at Barcelona during the period when the alleged, unproved, time-barred refereeing scandal happened, but not implicated or punished. He was at Air Spain when it collapsed, but cleared of any wrongdoing. And now he’s been at City in the period of inflated income that has, in effect, left the club dangling over the edge of a cliff. It is certainly an unfortunate chain of coincidence.‘Throw your medals in the bin,’ Roy Keane tells Manchester City playersRead moreOthers who will be asked what they knew, or not asked because he’s not going to speak to you, include the owner, Sheikh Mansour. This has an added element. It speaks to the ultimate test, some way down the line, of fitness to run a football club. How is it possible to spend so much family money on this thing, to dole out what are in effect government contracts, and not know the actual process here?But let’s face it, we all knew really. Weren’t the sham dealings obvious? It was there even in the absence of furious statements of support from the independent directors at First Abu Dhabi Bank, Etihad Airways, Experience Abu Dhabi, Emirates Palace Hotel in Abu Dhabi, Aldar Properties of Abu Dhabi, Masdar Energy of Abu Dhabi, e& telecoms of Abu Dhabi. Come on, chaps. Stand up for the investment. No word either from Dude Wipes, the club’s official male-oriented toilet-paper partner. Although who knows, we may now be entering full Dude Wipes territory.We knew about the sportswashing aspect, knew that City was a soft-power vehicle for the state of Abu Dhabi, which has a record of alleged – and of course denied – human rights abuses and so on. And of course City’s fans must have known this too, or felt it on some level. It was there cooked into the blueprint, the sense of something brutally high-end but strangely cold.JG Ballard coined the phrase “the death of affect” to describe the institutionalising of public feeling, rage and triumph commodified as a spectator event. Some champion teams have a strut. City’s basic vibe was always closer to an unceasing V-sign. Perhaps there was even a buried unease here. No one really enjoys being treated as a glove puppet, even when it is done gently and with a hand held discreetly under the desk. On which note, Pep? Any other questions now? Is this a good time?Explore more on these topicsManchester CityPep GuardiolafeaturesShareReuse this content

title: ‘I am here more than ever’: Guardiola backs Manchester City owners over guilty verdicts | Manchester City | The Guardian
description: Pep Guardiola has thrown his support behind Manchester City after the club were found guilty of all charges of breaching Premier League financial rules over a nine-year period
Author: Will Unwin
Headline: Pep Guardiola has thrown his support behind Manchester City after the club were found guilty of all charges of breaching Premier League financial rules over a nine-year period
Content: Pep Guardiola with Khaldoon al-Mubarak after City’s 2024 title win. The club’s former manager told fans: ‘We will get through this together.’Photograph: Martin Rickett/PAView image in fullscreenPep Guardiola with Khaldoon al-Mubarak after City’s 2024 title win. The club’s former manager told fans: ‘We will get through this together.’Photograph: Martin Rickett/PAManchester City‘I am here more than ever’: Guardiola backs Manchester City owners over guilty verdicts‘I am, always have been, always will, be behind my club’Former City chair Bernstein calls for directors to quitWill UnwinandTom GarryWed 30 Sep 2026 09.39 EDTLast modified on Wed 30 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GooglePep Guardiola has thrown his support behind Manchester City after the clubwere found guiltyof all charges of breaching Premier League financial rules over a nine-year period, telling fans: “We will get through this together.”Guardiola left City in the summer after a trophy-laden decade in charge, with his first two seasons falling within the period investigated by the independent commission. The Spaniard remains a close ally of the chief executive, Ferran Soriano, who brought him to England, the pair having previously worked together at Barcelona. City maintain their innocence and are set to appeal against the decision before Friday’s deadline.“I want every singleManchester Cityfan across the world to know I am here; more than ever,” Guardiola posted on social media. “I am, always have been, always will, be behind my club, my owner, my chairman, Ferran, the players, staff, Enzo [Maresca] and you, our unique supporters. Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all.”Disguised funding and dishonest witnesses: key findings in Manchester City caseRead moreTwenty trophies were won in the 10 years Guardiola managed City and he was frequently asked about the charges that hung over the club for much of his tenure.
