The 55-year-old has consistently reiterated his faith in what he was told by the club’s Abu Dhabi ownership while the investigation was ongoing,with charges first brought against the club in February 2023. “I trust them,” Guardiola said in May. “I spoke with them and trust how they behave and how they did.”Upon Guardiola’s departure, it was confirmed that he would continue as a global ambassador for City Football Group, which involves him giving “technical advice to the clubs in the group, working on specific projects and collaborations”.Meanwhile the former City chair David Bernstein has described the situation at the club as “beyond awful” and called for the board to stand down. “I can’t think of a penalty strong enough for this, really. I mean, this is absolutely terrible,” said Bernstein, who was chair between 1998 and 2003.“I want to raise another question, and that is the position of the board of directors. Because the directors ‌of the club, including the chief executive, who’s been there for years and went ‌through this period, are responsible for the running of the club in every respect.“If this was a public company of some sort, the directors would have to stand down or be suspended pending the outcome of all this, appeal or no appeal. I don’t ‌think the present management can credibly continue.”Andrée Jeglertz, the Manchester City Women’s head coach, insisted that it had been a case of “business as usual” for his team as they prepare to host Real Madrid in the Women’s Champions League on Thursday. Asked if he echoed Guardiola’s position and if he would back the club in spite of the Premier League’s guilty verdict, Jeglertz said: “Definitely. I’m working [at] this club now, and that’s definitely what I’m hired for, for sure.”The Swede declined to comment further when asked if he had been given any assurances that the women’s team would not be affected by the matter.Jeglertz insisted his side, whowon the Women’s Super League title last season, were focused only on football, saying: “We haven’t changed anything, we just keep on doing everything we normally do.”Explore more on these topicsManchester CityPep GuardiolanewsShareReuse this content

title: Hampton’s heroics preserve WCL point for Chelsea on Bompastor’s OL Lyonnes return | Women's Champions League | The Guardian
description: Hannah Hampton made a crucial late save to ensure Chelsea left OL Lyonnes with a 0-0 draw on Sonia Bompastor’s return to her former club
Author: Tom Garry
Headline: Hannah Hampton made a crucial late save to ensure Chelsea left OL Lyonnes with a 0-0 draw on Sonia Bompastor’s return to her former club
Content: Hannah Hampton at full stretch to deny Ada Hegerberg late on.Photograph: Olivier Chassignole/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenHannah Hampton at full stretch to deny Ada Hegerberg late on.Photograph: Olivier Chassignole/AFP/Getty ImagesWomen's Champions LeagueHampton’s heroics preserve WCL point for Chelsea on Bompastor’s OL Lyonnes returnTom Garryat Groupama StadiumWed 30 Sep 2026 17.11 EDTLast modified on Wed 30 Sep 2026 19.02 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThere were plenty of encouraging signs for Chelsea as they claimed a valuable point in the Champions League on their head coach Sonia Bompastor’s return to face her former teamOL Lyonnes.The goalless draw was a slow-burner but concluded with a flurry of late action where both teams missed chances to steal the points. However a draw felt fair on a night when Chelsea’s double pivot of Keira Walsh and Lexi Potter in midfield continued to flourish, three days after they similarly impressed inSunday’s victory over Arsenal.Leah Williamson blunder gifts Paris FC a point as Arsenal’s struggles continueRead moreOL Lyonnes had scored eight times in their first fixture in the league phase, away against the Swiss side Servette, but Chelsea looked comfortable for large periods and Bompastor said: “I’m really proud of my team, being able to not concede here. We are happy also with the ball, the way we performed, we were able to exploit different spaces. The only thing that was missing was the goal.”The French side had scored at least seven times in all four matches they had played in all competitions this season. Given that formidable form and the confidence in the hosts’ front line, Chelsea were grateful to Hannah Hampton for her sharp save from Salma Paralluelo on 20 minutes, and similarly glad to see Melchie Dumornay’s powerful effort fizz just wide of a post a few minutes later.Chelsea had the majority of the ball, however. Potter, buoyed by the receipt of her first senior England call-up on Tuesday, gave as good as she got in the physical battle in midfield and generally appeared at home on this stage, at the record eight-time European champions, which will have been pleasing for Sarina Wiegman. The 20-year-old, alongside her compatriot Walsh, helped Chelsea maintain an element of control.Unlike Chelsea, who played a fiery derby against Arsenal in England, the top French sides were able to rest at the weekend, in between the first two European fixtures, as the French league helps its sides stay fresh for the Champions League. Other French top-tier sides played in the League Cup instead. It was therefore reasonable to assume that Lyonnes might look the stronger as this contest went on. That was true to a degree, as Chelsea – missing Katie McCabe through illness – tired slightly late on.Quick GuideWCL roundup: Barcelona win big againShowBarcelonacontinued their emphatic start to their title defence by brushing asideRoma6-0 in the Italian capital. Caroline Graham Hansen got Barça off the mark in Rome inside 20 minutes. A Shukurat Oladipo own goal put them two up before the break and Clàudia Pina (pictured) made the points safe just after, before Graham Hansen and Pina both got their second goals and Ewa Pajor put the cherry on the cake late on.Bayern Munich, who gave up a two-goal lead last week to draw with Manchester City, were in danger of behind held again atBenfica, but won 3-0 thanks to three goals from in the last 16 minutes from Klara Bühl, Pernille Harder and Franziska Kett.JuventusdownedHäcken3-0 in Sweden to make up for  last Tuesday’s defeat by Benfica. The Spanish World Cup winner Alba Redondo scored again, making it three goals in as many games and seven in 12 in all competitions since joining from Real Madrid.AFPPhotograph: Domenico Cippitelli/Shutterstock EditorialWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.It was Chelsea, however, who started the second period the brighter. They thought they deserved a penalty when Tarciane took out Sjoeke Nüsken at the far post, just as the Chelsea midfielder looked certain to score, but after a check on the monitor, the referee concluded that Lucy Bronze had been interfering with play from an offside position as the ball was crossed. Tarciane was booked for her challenge, nonetheless.Bompastor, who won this competition as a player and a manager with Lyonnes, brought on Lauren James to give her side a different forward dynamic with just over half an hour remaining, while Lyonnes introduced a former Ballon d’Or winner in Ada Hegerberg, but neither side looked likely to break the deadlock until much later, as the off-the-ball qualities of both teams appeared to cancel each other out. A cautious approach, from Chelsea in particular, was understandable; this was, by a significant distance, the toughest-looking fixture of their league-phase matches, against last season’s runners-up.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenChelsea’s Lexi Potter impressed on the big stage after her first England call-up.Photograph: Alexandre Dimou/ReutersLyonnes, owned by the London City Lionesses and Washington Spirit owner, Michele Kang, have high ambitions to win this title this term. They thought they had scored on 72 minutes, when Paralluelo struck a low shot into the bottom corner, but the offside flag was raised.Just a few minutes later, a moment of real controversy arose, as Chelsea were awarded a penalty for a foul by Damaris Egurrola on James. After a video review, the decision was overturned with the referee appearing to conclude that James had made contact with Egurrola rather than the other way around. The Lyonnes midfielder, though, looked very fortunate to escape, having mistimed her tackle and also missed the ball completely. Chelsea were exasperated. Bompastor said later that she felt it was a “clear penalty”.James had Chelsea’s best chance late on but her close-range strike was blocked by Mala Grohs in goal, before Hampton saved superbly from Hegerberg at the other end, as the match finally came to life in the very late stages and Maika Hamano dragged a shot wide deep into stoppage time. But Chelsea will be satisfied with this point.Explore more on these topicsWomen's Champions LeagueOL LyonnesChelsea WomenWomen's footballmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: ‘I like him as a No 9’: Bellingham a striking alternative for England, says Tuchel | England | The Guardian
description: Thomas Tuchel’s hunt for alternatives to Harry Kane has led to him identifying Jude Bellingham as an option at No 9 for England
Author: Jacob Steinberg
Headline: Thomas Tuchel’s hunt for alternatives to Harry Kane has led to him identifying Jude Bellingham as an option at No 9 for England
Content: Jude Bellingham wore the captain’s armband after coming off the bench against Czechia.Photograph: Martin Divisek/EPAView image in fullscreenJude Bellingham wore the captain’s armband after coming off the bench against Czechia.Photograph: Martin Divisek/EPAEngland‘I like him as a No 9’: Bellingham a striking alternative for England, says TuchelHead coach sees Real Madrid man as an option up frontKane praises Alexander-Arnold’s impact and work rateJacob SteinbergWed 30 Sep 2026 14.00 EDTLast modified on Wed 30 Sep 2026 16.01 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThomas Tuchel’s hunt for alternatives to Harry Kane has led to him identifying Jude Bellingham as an option at No 9 for England. Kane continued his remarkable scoring record in the2-0 win against Czechiain the Nations League on Tuesday, moving to 87 goals in 123 international appearances with a late strike in Prague, but he has little cover up front.There is no prospect yet of Tuchel having to consider life without Kane. TheEnglandhead coach backed the 33-year-old striker to last another decade at the highest level, tipped him to reach a century of international goals soon, and said England cannot expect to produce a replica of their greatest forward. However, there is concern over whether England have enough depth in attack.Alexander-Arnold proves his worth to England with trademark assist against Czechia | Jacob SteinbergRead moreOllie Watkins and Ivan Toney have been overlooked for this camp. Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who came on for Kane during thedefeat by Spainon Saturday, is 29 and has four goals in 13 caps. Liam Delap, the 23-year-old Nottingham Forest forward, is yet to earn a senior call-up and it was noted that Bellingham led the line after coming on for Kane in the closing stages against Czechia.“You will not get anotherHarry Kane, first of all,” Tuchel said. “We look for different solutions. We finished the game with Jude as a No 9. There will be someone else but it will not be Harry or a copy of Harry. We will find a solution when it comes to it but maybe not me. It might be another 10 years.”Bellingham wore the captain’s armband after coming off the bench in Prague on Tuesday. “I like him as a [No] 9,” Tuchel said. “Then he can contribute to both sides and overloads the sides and doesn’t affect so much of the balance. We found a bit of a new role for him in the last match, as a central [No] 10, so he can go to both sides and it is more of a 4-2-3-1 than a 4-3-3 to have Harry and Jude closer together and to give them a chance to overload both sides.“We are working on that. Jude in general should always be able to go through the last line and be able to end up in the box. He is a natural goalscorer and has the hunger to be on the scoreboard. He wants to have the decisive action so it makes not a huge difference if he plays as a [No] 9 or a [No] 10.”England moved second inNations LeagueGroup A3 after seeing off Czechia, who were reduced to 10 men midway through the first half. Anthony Gordon opened the scoring and Kane finished well late on.“The ball falls down and you see Harry taking the shot and that is exactly the player you want it to drop down to,” Tuchel said. “He does it in every single match. The highest level of finishing.”Tuchel was the manager who took Kane to Bayern Munich in 2023. Uli Hoeness, Bayern’s honorary president, has since said the former Tottenham striker is the club’s greatest signing. “That is so beautiful as it tells me everyone can see his true value and his personality,” Tuchel said. “It is not easy to change and to come to Bayern Munich when you win, win, win and it is a big club. You are under the spotlight and he won everyone over.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionEngland’s next assignment is a trip to Rijeka to face Croatia on Saturday. It remains to be seen if Tuchel sticks with Trent Alexander-Arnold after the right-back marked his first international appearance since June 2025 by creating Gordon’s goal.“Trent’s outstanding,” Kane said. “The delivery, the passing range, the crossing but also today defensively he was outstanding. He’s a fantastic player. Trent just has to keep his head down, keep working hard. He’s been great in camp so far. He’s showing to the boss that he wants to be here.”Explore more on these topicsEnglandThomas TuchelJude BellinghamHarry KaneNations LeaguenewsShareReuse this content

title: Leah Williamson blunder gifts Paris FC a point as Arsenal’s struggles continue | Women's Champions League | The Guardian
description: Arsenal threw away a 2-0 lead to draw 2-2 in their Women’s Champions League game at Paris FC, a mix-up between Leah Williamson and Misa Rodríguez costing them dearly
Author: Suzanne Wrack
Headline: Arsenal threw away a 2-0 lead to draw 2-2 in their Women’s Champions League game at Paris FC, a mix-up between Leah Williamson and Misa Rodríguez costing them dearly
Content: Maeline Mendy (centre) gets a handshake from Kaja Korosec after scoring Paris FC’s equaliser.Photograph: Catherine Steenkeste/ReutersView image in fullscreenMaeline Mendy (centre) gets a handshake from Kaja Korosec after scoring Paris FC’s equaliser.Photograph: Catherine Steenkeste/ReutersWomen's Champions LeagueLeah Williamson blunder gifts Paris FC a point as Arsenal’s struggles continueSuzanne WrackWed 30 Sep 2026 15.31 EDTLast modified on Wed 30 Sep 2026 19.02 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleRenée Slegers did not attend the post‑match press conference, the manager understood to have been too furious after Arsenal threw away a two-goal lead in their draw withParis FCon Wednesday night.The assistant coach Aaron D’Antino stepped in to speak to the media instead of Slegers, after a disastrous mix-up between the goalkeeper Misa Rodríguez and the centre-back Leah Williamson gifted Paris FC a penalty that Maeline Mendy converted to deny Arsenal all three points in the Champions League.Hampton’s heroics preserve WCL point for Chelsea on Bompastor’s OL Lyonnes returnRead more“The most frustrating part is how much we are working behind the scenes to try and turn this around, and it is just not going our way at the moment,” D’Antino said.Alessia Russo and Georgia Stanway had given the Gunners a two-goal lead but Clara Mateo pulled one back before Williamson handled the ball after the referee deemed play to have restarted from a goal-kick when Rodríguez passed it to her.D’Antino said: “If we’re looking at what we can control, it’s just passing the ball to Leah. From what I remember seeing, the ball was still rolling and she was moving it to Leah for her to take the goal-kicks as we normally do. So maybe the learning in that is how we get the ball to Leah, so we don’t put ourselves in that situation. But as far as we’re concerned, that’s not a penalty … we haven’t taken a goal-kick, there’s no advantage gained by Leah stopping the ball.”It has been a tough start to the season for Arsenal, who are up against it in the title race with only five points from their opening four games, and the closing stages of the match in Paris delivered another gut punch.Quick GuideWCL roundup: Barcelona win big againShowBarcelonacontinued their emphatic start to their title defence by brushing asideRoma6-0 in the Italian capital. Caroline Graham Hansen got Barça off the mark in Rome inside 20 minutes. A Shukurat Oladipo own goal put them two up before the break and Clàudia Pina (pictured) made the points safe just after, before Graham Hansen and Pina both got their second goals and Ewa Pajor put the cherry on the cake late on.Bayern Munich, who gave up a two-goal lead last week to draw with Manchester City, were in danger of behind held again atBenfica, but won 3-0 thanks to three goals from in the last 16 minutes from Klara Bühl, Pernille Harder and Franziska Kett.JuventusdownedHäcken3-0 in Sweden to make up for  last Tuesday’s defeat by Benfica. The Spanish World Cup winner Alba Redondo scored again, making it three goals in as many games and seven in 12 in all competitions since joining from Real Madrid.AFPPhotograph: Domenico Cippitelli/Shutterstock EditorialWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Paris FC had promised another tricky test, with teams that are happy to concede possession frustrating an Arsenal side that just cannot seem to find their way through low blocks. Chelsea hadread that script on Sunday: they were organised at the back and punished Arsenal’s profligacy and failure to make their early dominance count.At the Stade Jean-Bouin, which sits in the shadow of Paris Saint-Germain’s Parc des Princes, the story was familiar. As a result, it was less a wave of relief that swept through the pocket of travelling Arsenal fans and the players when their first goal went in and more a tsunami. It had looked as if Arsenal’s hesitancy had cost them a possible opening again when Stanway prodded the ball towards Russo but the England forward took several touches to create the space to shoot before firing her low effort in.With the home team forced to come out more, that it took only five minutes after the restart for Arsenal to double their lead was no surprise. It was a stylish finish from Stanway that gave Arsenal breathing space, the midfielder pushed Emily Fox’s cross forward a little with her chest before lashing a volley in from close range.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenGeorgia Stanway is embraced after scoring Arsenal’s second goal before their evening took a turn for the worse.Photograph: Catherine Steenkeste/ReutersHowever, only 22 minutes of comfort followed, before the team that inflicted a shock win on penalties to knock Arsenal out of qualifying in 2023 pulled the goal back that would test the Gunners’ resolve.It was a mix-up between the centre-backs Lotte Wubben-Moy and Williamson that delivered the goal. The pair both moved to close down Evelyne Viens and the Canadian forward slipped the ball wide to Clara Mateo who raced free, rounded Rodríguez and slotted into the empty net.Paris FC 2-2 Arsenal: Women’s Champions League – liveRead moreIt was tense as the clock ticked down. Paris posed a threat throughout, but the leveller followed the most calamitous of mistakes by Arsenal. Rodríguez collected the ball for a goal-kick, rolled it on to the pitch and then passed it to Williamson who bent and stopped the ball with her hand. The referee’s whistle went and she pointed to the spot, with Rodríguez deemed to have taken the goal-kick while Williamson clearly assumed she was being given the ball to take it. VAR did not intervene and Mendy converted from the spot, driving powerfully into the bottom corner.It was a bruising end to another bruising game for Arsenal, who really need some luck to go their way to lift the increasing pressure. Meanwhile, Slegers’s decision to avoid talking after the game will have only ramped that pressure up further ahead of a must-win game against league leaders Manchester City on Sunday.Explore more on these topicsWomen's Champions LeagueParis FCArsenal WomenWomen's footballmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Craig Bellamy urges Wales improvement but wary of Norway’s threat | Wales | The Guardian
description: Wales were ‘unrecognisable’ in defeat against Denmark, Craig Bellamy said, while Norway’s Kristoffer Ajer said Erling Haaland had been ‘exactly the same’ after the Manchester City verdict
Author: Ben Fisher
Headline: Wales were ‘unrecognisable’ in defeat against Denmark, Craig Bellamy said, while Norway’s Kristoffer Ajer said Erling Haaland had been ‘exactly the same’ after the Manchester City verdict
Content: Craig Bellamy took the blame for Wales’s 2-0 defeat against Denmark in Copenhagen.Photograph: Ulrik Pedersen/NurPhoto/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenCraig Bellamy took the blame for Wales’s 2-0 defeat against Denmark in Copenhagen.Photograph: Ulrik Pedersen/NurPhoto/ShutterstockWalesCraig Bellamy urges Wales improvement but wary of Norway’s threatWales ‘unrecognisable’ in defeat against DenmarkHaaland ‘exactly the same’ after Manchester City verdictBen FisherWed 30 Sep 2026 13.11 EDTLast modified on Wed 30 Sep 2026 17.14 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleCraig Bellamy has said Wales must improve against Norway on Thursday after appearing unrecognisable in theirdefeat against Denmark, and highlighted their next opponents’ run to the World Cup quarter-finals as proof of their talent.Wales host Norway in Cardiff hoping to record their first win since last November and their first since promotion toNations LeagueA. “This team has been on a surge,” he said of Ståle Solbakken’s side. “They are progressing and they will keep going as well – they ain’t going away, especially with the youngsters they’ve got coming through. We’ve all been waiting [for them to flourish]. But it was coming and it’s come with a bang.”Denmark dominate Wales in Nations League to leave Bellamy ‘really hurting’Read moreBellamy said Norway having two teams in the Champions League – Bodø/Glimt and Viking – would have been a “miracle a number of years ago”. Addressing the Norwegian media at his pre-match press conference on Wednesday, Bellamy said: “I think you’re all sneakily hoping we don’t talk about you as much butthe World Cupexposes you. But I’m on to yous. I know what you’re up to and I know your younger age groups are getting even stronger.“Sander [Berge], [Martin] Ødegaard and [Erling] Haaland, they are really close friends and their three sons are all the same age, born within a few months of each other. They’re already preparing the next generation, so we’re all in trouble.”Addressing Wales’s 2-0 defeat in Copenhagen on Sunday, Bellamy said: “I didn’t recognise anything about us in the game and that was hard. We didn’t look clear in what we were doing, we were ‘in between’ and that comes from myself. I want us to improve as a team and I want to improve.”Meanwhile, the Brentford defender Kristoffer Ajer insisted Haaland has displayed the same personality as normal amid the noise surrounding Manchester City after the club were found guilty ofbreaching the Premier League’s financial rules across a nine-year period. “Ever since I met him he’s been a guy that brings a lot of energy and joy to the group and that’s the biggest compliment I always give Erling,” Ajer said.“When people ask about him, he hasn’t changed one bit since the first time I met him, even though he’s the biggest star on the planet right now. He’s been exactly the same the last few days as well, which is not a surprise for me.”Solbakken, Norway’s head coach for the past six years, said “everything’s fine” with Haaland, who has scored three goals in his past two matches, and played down the idea that the City verdict has been a distraction. “[He’s been] very good, scoring goals,” Solbakken said.“He missed one chance against Portugal that he usually doesn’t miss and that’s the only thing I can say negative, because he’s on fire.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionBellamy said he did not expect Haaland to be bothered by his club’s situation at Cardiff City Stadium. The Wales head coach said: “I don’t think he’ll be distracted, the guy’s a machine. Have you seen his record at international level? He’s brilliant. If you love football, you have to appreciate him … You see certain moments in certain sports. Remember the Jonah Lomu factor [in rugby union]? We’re coming through the Haaland factor at this present moment.”Ødegaard is a doubt for the game on Thursday after a poor challenge by Bernardo Silva in the 2-1 defeat by Portugal on Sunday. “He will probably test himself a bit today,” Solbakken said of the Arsenal and Norway captain before training in the Welsh capital. “If he had no chance [of playing], he wouldn’t be here.”Explore more on these topicsWalesCraig BellamyErling HaalandNorwayManchester CityNations LeaguenewsShareReuse this content

title: Cristiano Ronaldo walks out on Portugal after being dropped from starting lineup | Cristiano Ronaldo | The Guardian
description: With Jorge Jesus, the Portugal coach, saying Cristiano Ronaldo would again be a substitute against Denmark, the 41-year-old has left the team’s training camp
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: With Jorge Jesus, the Portugal coach, saying Cristiano Ronaldo would again be a substitute against Denmark, the 41-year-old has left the team’s training camp
Content: Cristiano Ronaldo was left on the bench against Norway and was set to be a substitute once more against Denmark.Photograph: Johan Nilsson/TT/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenCristiano Ronaldo was left on the bench against Norway and was set to be a substitute once more against Denmark.Photograph: Johan Nilsson/TT/ShutterstockCristiano RonaldoCristiano Ronaldo walks out on Portugal after being dropped from starting lineupJorge Jesus earlier said captain would again be a subThe 41-year-old has trained alone in gym since weekendAgence France-PresseWed 30 Sep 2026 15.55 EDTFirst published on Wed 30 Sep 2026 10.01 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Portugal captain,Cristiano Ronaldo, announced on Wednesday that he had left the team’s training camp in Denmark after head coach Jorge Jesus told reporters that the iconic striker would not start their next match.Ronaldo had been due to train with his teammates at the Parken Stadium in Copenhagen on Wednesday but left abruptly after Jesus’s press conference. The veteran coach had said that Ronaldo, who spent the entire match on the bench against Norway on Sunday, would not start Thursday’sNations Leagueclash away to Denmark either.Nations League roundup: Lamine Yamal sinks Croatia in Spain’s World Cup homecomingRead more“Following the national team coach’s press conference, and after having a conversation with the Portuguese Football Federation president, I decided to leave the national team’s training camp,” Ronaldo wrote on Instagram. “In due course, I will tell the truth to all the Portuguese people about my reasons for leaving the national team, to which I have always been dedicated.“Now is time to wish good luck toPortugaland to all my teammates, without exception.”Jesus had insisted earlier that there was no rift between him and Ronaldo, although the 72-year-old did acknowledge that his captain had been disappointed to remain on the bench in the side’s Nations League win over Norway.Following the 2-1 victory in Oslo, Ronaldo went straight to the changing rooms without joining his teammates in acknowledging the Portuguese supporters in the stands. “There was no incident whatsoever,” Jesus told reporters.“Any player – and I was a player myself … when you spend 20 or 30 minutes warming up and then don’t get on … no one is happy about that,” Jesus said on Wednesday.The Portuguese coach added that he had told Ronaldo before the match that he would not be in the starting lineup, but that he might bring him on towards the end of the game.“Afterwards, as coach, I decided not to bring him on. It’s nothing to make a fuss about,” Jesus insisted. The former Benfica manager also explained that Ronaldo had not refused to train on Tuesday, as some Portuguese media outlets had suggested, but that he had had to do individual exercises for physical “mobility” and “strengthening”.Jesus had said that the five-time Ballon d’Or winner would train as normal on Wednesday. However, despite arriving at the stadium in the team bus, Ronaldo did not join his teammates on the pitch. Portuguese media shared a video of him leaving Parken alongside two members of the backroom staff just after Jesus’s press conference. Reports also said that Ronaldo’s private jet was heading to Copenhagen. Just before Ronaldo’s social media post, the Portuguese federation had released a brief statement merely confirming that the former Real Madrid, Manchester United and Juventus player had not trained.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionJesus had said earlier that for the Denmark match he again intended to start the Milan striker Gonçalo Ramos, who scored the winner against Norway.“If everything goes according to plan, it will be Gonçalo who plays,” he said, before adding regarding Ronaldo: “If I need him, he’ll come on. If I don’t need him, he won’t.”At 41, Ronaldo announced this summer that this season would “probably [be] my last year in football”. He is Portugal’s leading goalscorer and most capped player, with 146 goals in 234 appearances.Explore more on these topicsCristiano RonaldoPortugalNations LeaguenewsShareReuse this content

title: City sponsor Etihad Airways considering legal action against the Premier League | Manchester City | The Guardian
description: Manchester City’s main sponsor, Etihad Airways, is considering legal action against the Premier League after the verdict of the independent commission
Author: Matt Hughes
Headline: Manchester City’s main sponsor, Etihad Airways, is considering legal action against the Premier League after the verdict of the independent commission
Content: Etihad Airways claimed the Premier League failed to consult the airline throughout their investigation.Photograph: Alan Smith/AlamyView image in fullscreenEtihad Airways claimed the Premier League failed to consult the airline throughout their investigation.Photograph: Alan Smith/AlamyManchester CityCity sponsor Etihad Airways considering legal action against the Premier LeagueAirline ‘categorically rejects’ commission’s guilty verdictEtihad has been club’s principal shirt sponsor since 2009Matt HughesWed 30 Sep 2026 17.30 EDTLast modified on Wed 30 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleManchester City’s main sponsor, Etihad Airways, is considering legal action against the Premier League following its publication of the independent commission’s core decision onmore than 100 findings of financial rule breachesby the club.In a statement released on Wednesday evening, Etihad said it “categorically rejects” the guilty verdicts of the independent commission, which it claimed had “damaging implications” for the airline, despite not being named in the published report.The independent commission found City guilty of artificially inflating their revenues by £900m through “sham” sponsorship contracts that were secretly funded by the owners, the Abu Dhabi United Group.Building of the Pep supremacy is an era that will be defined by sham-ballRead moreEtihad, the state-owned national airline of the United Arab Emirates, has been City’s principal shirt sponsor since 2009 and was the main source of the initial transformation of their revenues. In 2011 City announced a 10-year naming rights deal worth £400m for the Etihad Stadium, which was subsequently extended on improved terms in 2021.“Etihad Airways has reviewed the Premier League commission’s published opinion relating to the disciplinary proceedings involvingManchester City, together with the Premier League’s public communication of its findings,” the statement said. “Etihad categorically rejects any finding, conclusion or implication that suggests the airline has ever been involved in improper commercial arrangements.“The Premier League’s public communication of the commission’s findings, following a period of selective leaks and reporting, has further created damaging implications for Etihad despite the airline not being named in the redacted published findings.”Etihad repeated the phrase used by the City chief executive, Ferran Soriano, in his extraordinary video sent to staff, that the commission’s ruling is an “opinion”, and claimed the Premier League failed to consult the airline throughout their investigation.“At no time did the Premier League reach out to or engage with Etihad in the process associated with the commission’s opinion,” it said. “Etihad was therefore never given the opportunity by the Premier League to be represented, to provide relevant information, or to ensure the accuracy and fairness of information relied upon in reaching conclusions that may now be interpreted as reflecting adversely on the airline.“Etihad is deeply concerned by the way this matter has been communicated publicly. The lack of clarity and transparency, together with the selective disclosure of information, has created damaging implications for Etihad despite the airline not being named in the published decision. The Premier League must take responsibility for the consequences of the way in which these findings have been presented.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“Etihad is immensely proud of its longstanding relationship with Manchester City. The Etihad name has been proudly carried by the club and its stadium for many years, as part of a partnership that has connected us with millions of supporters around the world. Our commitment to Manchester City, its supporters and our shared partnership remains strong.“We stand with the club, its supporters and our wider Etihad community as Manchester City challenges the commission’s conclusions through the processes available to it. Etihad will seek the relevant legal counsel on the options and recourse available to protect its interests.”Explore more on these topicsManchester CityPremier LeaguenewsShareReuse this content

title: Manchester City whistleblower Rui Pinto no longer a protected witness in Portugal | Manchester City | The Guardian
description: Pinto’s work provided information concerning Manchester City’s finances and he called the decision on their charges ‘historic for English football’
Author: Ed Aarons
Headline: Pinto’s work provided information concerning Manchester City’s finances and he called the decision on their charges ‘historic for English football’
Content: Rui Pinto has been told to ‘exercise caution with family’ and avoid social media after being told he is not a protected witness any more.Composite: Manchester City FC/AFP via Getty Images; Manchester City FC via Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenRui Pinto has been told to ‘exercise caution with family’ and avoid social media after being told he is not a protected witness any more.Composite: Manchester City FC/AFP via Getty Images; Manchester City FC via Getty ImagesManchester CityManchester City whistleblower Rui Pinto no longer a protected witness in PortugalWork provided information concerning City’s financesHe called City decision ‘historic for English football’Ed AaronsandMiguel DantasWed 30 Sep 2026 15.40 EDTLast modified on Wed 30 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleRui Pinto, whose leaks of private documents helped to trigger the Premier League’s investigation into Manchester City’s financial affairs, will no longer be protected as a witness by the Portuguese authorities, it can be revealed. The removal of the whistleblower’s protection was decided on Wednesday, according to documents seen by the Guardian.Pinto has also been advised to “exercise caution with family contacts” and avoid social media. The 37-year-old, who is the man behind the website Football Leaks, has been a protected witness since 2020, after agreeing to grant Portuguese authorities access to millions of files gathered before his arrest.Rival clubs feel relegating Manchester City to Championship would not be enoughRead moreThe Portuguese police have deemed the risk to Pinto’s safety to be low, despite an assault on him in Lisbon in April and the ongoing fallout from the City investigation. It is understood that Pinto was left with a bruised eyebrow after the incident and the police were informed, although no complaint was filed.Pinto was handed a suspended four-year sentence in September 2023 after being found guilty on counts of attempted extortion, illegal access to data and breach of correspondence. But he has been hailed as a hero by some supporters for exposing millions of confidential documents linked to some of the biggest clubs, players and organisations in world football. That included providing information concerning City’s finances, which was passed to the German publication Der Spiegel and its partners in the European Investigative Collaborations network and led to Uefa and thePremier Leagueopening separate investigations.While City eventually overturned their Champions League ban via the court of arbitration for sport, they were found guilty of 114charges spanning nine seasonsby the Premier League on Tuesday having been accused of disguising over £900m in funding through sham commercial contracts and false accounting. The deadline for City to appeal is on Friday.Pinto has been heavily active on social media since reports that City had been found guilty emerged last week. He described it as a “historic decision for English football” and took aim at City’s executives in another post, who he said had “acted with complete impunity, challenging everyone and everything”, saying: “From the very beginning, they have demonstrated a complete lack of respect for the rules, for the bodies responsible for overseeing and regulating the game, for the integrity of the competition, for the other clubs and, above all, for the fans. Years and years of cheating, lying and manipulation will finally have consequences.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionHours before confirmation that he will no longer be a protected witness emerged, Pinto also accused the Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, of having done “everything in his power” to ensure that City and Paris Saint-Germain would only be fined for contravening Uefa’s FFP rules when he was general secretary at European football’s governing body.Explore more on these topicsManchester CityPremier LeaguenewsShareReuse this content
